ety.text: Borrowed from Middle French loyal, from Old French loial, leial, leal, from Latin lēgālis. Doublet of legal and leal.

senses.d: Having or demonstrating undivided and constant support for someone or something.
ex: Dogs are very loyal animals, which is why they make wonderful pets.
George is a loyal and loving husband.

senses.d: Firm in allegiance to a person or institution; allegiant.
Faithful to a person or cause.
ex: We must remain loyal to the mission.

grp.label: firm in allegiance to a person or institution

ety.text: Inherited from Old French loial (with various alternative forms: leial, leal, loyel) from Latin lēgālis. Equivalent to loi + -al. Doublet of légal.
Borrowed from Latin fidēlis (“loyal”), replaced the inherited Old French fedel, fëel (cf. French féal).
Borrowed from Old Occitan or Old French leial, from Latin legālis, whence also the doublet legale.
Borrowed from Old French lige; see English liege.

es:leal.gl: adhering to the rules of propriety, fair, honest, loyal, true

ety.text: Inherited from Old Spanish, from Latin lēgālis. See also the borrowed doublet legal.

pt:leal.gl: adhering to the rules of propriety, fair, honest, loyal, true

ety.text: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese leal, from Latin legālis. Doublet of legal. By surface analysis, lei + -al. Compare Spanish leal, Catalan lleial, French loyal.
From Old Galician-Portuguese fiel, from Latin fidēlis.
From Middle English loialte, borrowed from Old French loialte, loiauté (Modern loyauté) from loial + -té, equivalent to loyal + -ty.

senses.d: The state of being loyal; fidelity.
Faithfulness or devotion to some person, cause or nation.
ex: He showed loyalty to his local football club after successive relegations.

grp.label: the state of being loyal; fidelity
faithfulness or devotion to some person, cause or nation

ety.text: Inherited from Middle French loyaulte, from Old French loiauté (whence English loyalty), leialté, possibly corresponding to Medieval Latin lēgālitās, lēgālitātem, from Latin lēgālis. Compare Spanish lealtad, Portuguese lealdade, Italian lealtà.
From leale + -ità; cf. Old French leialté.
Inherited from Latin fidēlitātem. Doublet of fidelità, a borrowing.

From lealdad, from leal + -dad, possibly corresponding to Medieval Latin legalitās, legalitātem, from Latin legālis. By surface analysis, leal + -tad. Compare Portuguese lealdade, French loyauté, Italian lealtà. Doublet of legalidad.
From Old Galician-Portuguese lealdade, from Medieval Latin lēgālitātem, from Latin lēgālis. By surface analysis, leal + -dade. Doublet of legalidade.
